metadata.case_name: LI SAI HUNG v. TSUI KWONG WAI

plaintiff.occupation_after: Returned to the same work (Post Office); restricted to sedentary employment for life
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: Restricted to sedentary employment for life

injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: A fracture of the right forearm
source: A fracture of the right forearm

injuries.icd_description: Fracture of lumbar spine or pelvis, unspecified

injuries.description: Permanent disability of the left leg
source: He has however a permanent disability of the left leg.

manifestations.description: Pain and stiffness in the neck
There is some residual weakness in the right wrist which should disappear
a scar, which is not very noticeable, on the forehead
Left leg shorter than the right, healed in a slightly twisted position resulting in the left foot being turned inwards
Walks with a distinct limp; cannot run; ascends and descends stairs with difficulty
All vigorous athletic pursuits are now out of the question; swimming limited to recreational bathing only
Driving not advisable at present because of pain from the hip region and neck when turning to see when reversing
Restricted to sedentary employment for life
Absent from work for six months altogether
Wore an orthopaedic collar initially all day and still wears for a short time each day

treatments_received: Admitted to Queen Mary Hospital on 13th November, 1977
The fracture of the hip was treated by operative reduction and fixed with nail, boneplate and serews.
The fractures of the forearm and pelvis were treated conservatively
Readmitted April 1978 for further X-Rays including a Myelogram
treatments_future: Removal of the nail and boneplate in his hip in the near future

losses.description: Permanent disability of the left leg: shorter than the right, healed in a slightly twisted position resulting in the left foot being turned inwards.
Walks with a distinct limp, cannot run, ascends and descends stairs with difficulty.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: All vigorous athletic pursuits are now out of the question; swimming limited to recreational bathing only; participation in outdoor activities severely limited.
A scar on the forehead which is not very noticeable.
Restricted to sedentary employment for life; may be unable to change to other careers in future.
